items.title: Confirm which workbook cells feed game values (yield, price, land rent, hauling, interest, crop insurance)
items.current_default: Named workbook column per field (budget_fields.col in pipeline/sources/regions/suwannee.json): yield Marketing!C7 (205 bu/A); gross price Marketing!C8 ($5.20/bu); net farm-gate price Marketing!C27 ($4.78/bu, paid by the market channel); crop insurance premium, Revenue Protection 75%, Marketing column D ($12.20/A, a separate cost); budget total net farm-gate crop revenue Marketing!D39 ($967.70/A, used only to reconcile); land rent FieldDetails!E19 ($285.71/A, rented only); own hauling Marketing!D22 ($0); operating interest OperatingRates!C22
items.notes: Spot-check 2026-10-20 found the first-numeric-cell rule read whole-farm rent (FieldDetails!D19 = $40,000) as $/acre; fixed by picking named columns, and validation rejects per-acre costs outside 0..revenue per acre. Resolved 2026-11-05 by project-owner decision (option C): the Marketing sheet shows gross revenue $1,066.00/A, minus buyer drying fees $24.60/A ($0.12/bu) and buying-point hauling $61.50/A ($0.30/bu), gives net farm-gate sales revenue C27 = $4.78/bu ($979.90/A); minus the crop insurance premium (Revenue Protection, 75%) of $12.20/A ($0.06/bu) gives total net farm-gate crop revenue C39 = $4.72/bu ($967.70/A). Additional crop revenues (insurance proceeds, farm program payments, crop residue) are $0. The game pays C27 and carries the premium as a separate, optional cost; validation checks yield x price - premium = D39. Owned and rented workbooks match on these rows.

items.title: Owned land: property tax, property insurance, maintenance/upkeep, and land appreciation
items.current_default: Not yet modelled. The 2026 owned budget carries $0 land rent (FieldDetails!E19) and $0 mortgage (FieldDetails!E20), but its BudgetSummary 'Land cost' is $12.00/A ($1,680 on 140 acres): FieldDetails 'Property tax and insurance' $10.00/A ($1,400) plus 'Fixed electric standby charge' $2.00/A ($280); opportunity cost $0. These two FieldDetails rows were read from the public workbook on 2026-11-09 by value order; their cells are confirmed by the next budgets fetch. Increment 2b models the $10.00/A as the cited property tax and property insurance lines (option C, 2026-11-09) and adds maintenance/upkeep; the $2.00/A standby charge is not an owned-land line

options.summary: Basic mode: one owned-land cost in $/acre/year, equal to the sum of the three Advanced lines (validated to +/- $0.01/A). With option C: $4.03 + $5.97 + $23.96 = $33.96/A/yr (values to be built and spot-checked)
Advanced mode: three lines - property tax (see owned-land-use-value), property insurance (see owned-land-insurance-proxy), maintenance/upkeep (see owned-land-upkeep-proxy)

items.notes: Decided 2026-10-20: owned land must carry property tax and other ownership costs, and must gain value over the period of ownership. Deferred 2026-11-02 (no approved source for Increment 2). Decided 2026-11-06 by the project owner: owned land necessarily includes a cost; Basic shows one average, Advanced shows property tax, property insurance and maintenance/upkeep separately, both read from the same data pack. Land appreciation is in scope for Increment 2b (see land-appreciation-method). Corrected 2026-11-09: earlier text said owned land has no land cost; the workbook overlap scan (see owned-land-upkeep-proxy) found the $12.00/A land cost described in current_default. Decided 2026-11-09 by the project owner (option C): property tax + property insurance must equal the owned budget's 'Property tax and insurance' ($10.00/A), so the game's owned-land tax and insurance match the budget the rest of the game uses. Status stays open until the values are built and spot-checked.

items.title: Owned land property tax: Suwannee County agricultural-use (greenbelt) value per acre and millage
items.current_default: Not yet modelled. Method: median agricultural classified-use assessed value per acre for all Suwannee County cropland parcels (DOR use codes 051-053; 050 excluded; no municipal filter), $278.63/A on the 2026 roll, x FY2026-27 total millage 14.4745 mills ($14.4745 per $1,000 of taxable value) = $4.03/A/yr
items.notes: Use value: fetched automatically (fetch step 'parcels', added 2026-11-07) from the Florida Statewide Parcels layer published by the State of Florida Geographic Information Office: the Florida Department of Revenue parcel GIS joined with the real property assessment roll (NAL) that the Suwannee County Property Appraiser submits to the Department. Filter CO_NO = 71 (Suwannee) and DOR_UC 051-053 (cropland, soil capability Class I-III; codes confirmed against the 2025 DOR NAL/SDF/NAP User's Guide). Value = AV_CLASS_USE (assessed value of the agriculturally classified portion) / parcel acres (LND_SQFOOT / 43,560); parcel acres include any non-classified portion such as a homesite, so values are conservative. Median, 25th/75th percentiles, counts by use code and taxing authority, and assessment year are written to parcels_summary.json; the sha256 of every query page is in fetch-lock.json. Only allow-listed value and land-use fields are requested: owner names, mailing addresses, parcel IDs and geometry are never downloaded. First fetch 2026-11-07 (run 42384231645, 2026 roll): 431 parcels, median $278.63/A (p25 $235.00, p75 $285.00; min $41.81, max $1,253.00); 051: 1 parcel, $277.53; 052: 240 parcels, $285.00; 053: 190 parcels, $234.99. Decided 2026-11-07 by the project owner: use all 431 parcels with no municipal filter, because TAX_AUTH_CD is 'CO' for every parcel and cannot separate Live Oak or Branford; exclude improved agricultural (050) parcels because they usually carry buildings. JV_CLASS_USE (median $2,000/A, p25 = p75 = $2,000) is not used. Optional: per-field tax by matching each SSURGO unit's capability class to a cropland code. Millage: decided 2026-11-07 by the project owner to use FY2026-27 rates, which are levied on the 2026 roll used here. Unincorporated Suwannee County FY2026-27: County 8.8000 (final budget hearing 2026-09-21); School Board 5.405 (required local effort 3.157 + discretionary 0.748 + capital outlay 1.500; final hearing 2026-09-08, resolution SCSB 2027-04R); Suwannee River Water Management District 0.2695 (Resolution 2026-14, final hearing 2026-09-21; the signed resolution has not been seen, only the staff recommendation and the Alachua County Property Appraiser's 2026 rate table); total 14.4745, which matches the Suwannee County Property Appraiser Tax Rates page. Property tax = $278.63 x 14.4745 / 1,000 = $4.03/A/yr. Superseded FY2025-26 rates: County 8.8000, School Board 5.415, SRWMD 0.2812, total 14.4962. Classification requires an application to the Property Appraiser by March 1 each year (possible Advanced-mode decision). Option C (2026-11-09, see owned-land-insurance-proxy): this property tax is also the first part of the owned budget's 'Property tax and insurance' ($10.00/A); property insurance is the remainder, so this line must stay at or below $10.00/A.

items.title: Owned land property insurance: remainder of the owned budget's 'Property tax and insurance' after property tax (ERS 'Taxes and insurance' kept as a cross-check)
items.current_default: Not yet modelled. Option C (project owner, 2026-11-09): property insurance = owned budget FieldDetails 'Property tax and insurance' ($10.00/A) - property tax line ($4.03/A, see owned-land-use-value) = $5.97/A/yr, a derived value cited to svaec-corn-2026-ct-owned and agroeco-adjustments. Validation: property tax + property insurance = the budget's 'Property tax and insurance' (+/- $0.01/A) and property insurance >= 0

options.summary: A: use the budget's $10.00/A as one tax-and-insurance line. Matches the budget, but Advanced mode would show two lines instead of three and the parcel/millage tax becomes a cross-check only. Not chosen

B: property tax $4.03/A (parcels x millage) + ERS 'Taxes and insurance' $17.02/A (2024). Every line independently cited, but $21.05/A is $11.05/A above the budget's $10.00/A and the ERS line includes machinery insurance. Not chosen
C: property tax $4.03/A (parcels x millage) + property insurance = remainder of the budget's $10.00/A ($5.97/A). Keeps three Advanced lines and reconciles to the budget. Chosen 2026-11-09

items.notes: Approved 2026-11-06 as an ERS-based flagged upper estimate; replaced 2026-11-09 by option C after the workbook overlap scan found that the owned budget already carries 'Property tax and insurance' of $10.00/A ($1,400 on 140 acres) in its $12.00/A land cost, so ERS insurance on top would double-count. Same reconcile-to-budget approach as the crop insurance premium decision of 2026-11-05. Weaknesses accepted: the $5.97/A is a remainder with no independent source, so any error in the budget's $10.00/A or in the $4.03/A tax lands in it; and it assumes the budget's line means real-estate tax plus property insurance on the land parcel, which the workbook does not document. If a future roll or millage puts property tax above $10.00/A, validation must fail rather than produce negative insurance. Cross-check: USDA ERS corn, Southern Seaboard, 'Taxes and insurance' = $17.02 per planted acre in 2024 (latest actual year in fetch run 42653191269; 2020-2024: 19.53, 13.92, 15.35, 16.03, 17.02; 2020 is on the 2016 survey base, 2021-2024 on the 2021 base). It is higher than $5.97/A, which is consistent with ERS including machinery insurance and non-real-estate property tax. Open question for the budget author (Kevin Athearn, UF/IFAS NFREC-Suwannee Valley, athearn@ufl.edu): what the $10.00/A 'Property tax and insurance' covers and how it was estimated.

items.title: Owned land maintenance/upkeep: USDA ERS 'General farm overhead' proxy
items.current_default: Not yet modelled. USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns, corn, Southern Seaboard region, 'General farm overhead', latest actual year 2024 = $23.96 per planted acre (fetch step 'ers', run 42653191269). Workbook overlap scan 2026-11-09: cleared for use, with the fixed electric standby charge excluded (see notes)
items.notes: Approved 2026-11-06. ERS general farm overhead covers utilities, supplies, maintenance of general-use structures and general business expense. For scale, the ERS 2026 U.S. forecast is $26.03 per planted acre. Fetched series 2020-2024: 29.34, 20.93, 23.40, 24.31, 23.96 (2020 on the 2016 survey base, 2021-2024 on the 2021 base). Condition (2026-11-06): before adding it, scan the SVAEC 2026 owned budget workbook (FieldCornBudget2026_Grain-Irrig-CT_Owned_260209.xlsx) for existing overhead, utilities, maintenance, tax or insurance lines, and the FieldOperations fixed costs for machinery depreciation, interest, repairs, taxes and insurance; if any overlap exists, stop and report it. Scan done 2026-11-09 on the public workbook (all sheets) and reported to the project owner the same day. Per acre, 140 acres: (1) Land cost $12.00/A ($1,680) = FieldDetails 'Property tax and insurance' $10.00/A ($1,400) + 'Fixed electric standby charge' $2.00/A ($280); rent, mortgage and opportunity cost $0. The tax and insurance part overlaps the property tax and insurance lines, not this one; resolved by option C (see owned-land-insurance-proxy). (2) The standby charge is a utility, which ERS overhead also covers: it is not an owned-land line and must not be charged separately while this line is used; revisit when irrigation is modelled. (3) Machinery ownership or lease $179.16/A, farm vehicle ownership or lease $6.80/A, irrigation and fertigation equipment $136.99/A (with its own 'Tax & Insurance' and 'Fixed Maintenance, Repair, or Service' columns), and variable maintenance and repairs $73.23/A cover machinery, vehicles and irrigation, not land or general-use buildings. The pack does not read them and Basic mode uses custom hire, so there is no overlap in Basic; they overlap ERS overhead and insurance in Advanced mode and must be reconciled then. (4) The budget states that gross profit does not include a cost for overall business management or general and administrative costs, so the general business expense in ERS overhead is not in the budget. Result: no overlap for this line in Basic mode apart from item (2). The FieldDetails rows in (1) were identified by value order in the downloaded workbook; their cells are confirmed when the next budgets fetch extracts the labels 'Land cost', 'Property tax and insurance', 'Fixed electric standby charge' and 'Opportunity cost'.

items.title: Owned land appreciation rate
items.current_default: Not yet modelled. Method: USDA NASS Land Values 2026 Summary, Florida cropland average value per acre, 2022-2026 ($8,340; $9,290; $10,170; $10,550; $11,100); compound average annual growth 2022-2026 = 7.41%/yr
items.notes: In scope for Increment 2b (data); applying appreciation in the game belongs to Increment 3. Year-on-year changes: 2023 +11.4%, 2024 +9.5%, 2025 +3.7%, 2026 +5.2%; the compound average over 2022-2026 is (11,100 / 8,340)^(1/4) - 1 = 7.41%/yr. Recent years are slower than the average, so this rate is on the high side. NASS publishes state values only, so this is a state-level estimate for a Suwannee County farm. Figures transcribed from the Land Values 2026 Summary (released July 31, 2026), Cropland Average Value per Acre table.

items.title: Basic vs. Advanced game modes: scope of Advanced mode
items.current_default: Basic mode: hired custom operations only; crop insurance rp-75 always bought; owned-land cost shown as one average. Advanced mode: not yet built
items.notes: Decided 2026-11-06: Advanced mode lets the player own machinery, hire workers, own farm trucks and own buildings, and see owned-land costs line by line; crop insurance becomes a player choice, which first needs Revenue Protection payouts modelled (USDA RMA projected and harvest prices plus a yield history). Approved order: Increment 2b (owned-land costs and appreciation), Increment 3 (UI-free engine, Basic end to end, with a basic/advanced mode switch from the start), then an Advanced-mode requirements step, then Advanced increments starting with machinery. Insurance researched for Advanced mode: workers' compensation is required for farm employers with 6 or more regular employees and/or 12 or more seasonal workers working more than 30 days in a season or more than 45 days in a calendar year (Florida DFS); registered vehicles with 4 or more wheels need at least $10,000 PIP and $10,000 property damage liability (FLHSMV); flood insurance is required on buildings in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area that secure a federally regulated or federally backed loan; lenders may require scheduled coverage on financed equipment. Common optional coverage: farm liability, farm property and machinery, umbrella, environmental, custom-farming liability, ATV/UTV, trailers, commercial auto. Machinery insurance estimate: about 0.5% of average machine value (Mississippi State P3543).
